Λ∆ʹ, ιθʹ": English quotes Job 34:19 but source passage ends at chapter 34 verse 19 marker without quoting text; English inserts alien verse; [completeness] "and he called down curses on himself" vs "καὶ ἑαυτῷ ἐπηράσατο": Greek says 'he cursed himself' not 'called down curses on himself'; but more critically, English adds 'since' clause for ἐπεστομίσθησαν but drops connective logic; [agency] "he called down curses on himself, since his friends had been silenced" vs "καὶ ἑαυτῷ ἐπηράσατο ὅτι ἐπεστομίσθησαν οἱ φίλοι": Greek: he cursed himself because the friends were silenced; English 'since' makes temporal not causal, and 'called down curses' overtranslates simple ἐπηράσατο; [modality] "I will give heed to you" vs "μέχρι ὑμῶν συνήσω": Greek 'until I understand you' not 'I will give heed to you'; wrong meaning of συνήσω; [agency] "not even when you were refuting me did you refute as you should have" vs "οὐδὲ ὅτε ἠλέγχετε, ὡς ἔδει, ἠλέγξατε": Greek has no 'me'; English adds object 'me' not in source; [modality] "or, later you fell silent" vs "ἢ ὅτι ὕστερον ἐσιωπήσατε": Greek 'or that later you were silent' (indicative fact), English 'fell silent' (inceptive); [completeness] "This is how he responds to" vs "Οὕτω πρὸς τό": Greek 'Thus toward the [saying]' not 'This is how he responds to'; English adds 'he responds'; [negation] "He did not think this" vs "οὐχὶ τοῦτο ἐνόμιζεν": Greek 'not this he-was-thinking' = 'he was not thinking this'; English correct; [agency] "Elihu supposed this, but Job did not speak with such a judgment" vs "τοῦτο μὲν γὰρ ὑπελάμβανεν ὁ Ἐλιοὺς, ἀλλ' οὐχὶ τοιαύτῃ γνώμῃ ὁ Ἰὼβ εἶπεν": Greek 'this indeed for Elihu supposed, but not with-such judgment Job spoke'; English 'but Job did not speak' corrects to finite verb but adds 'with such a judgment' slightly off; [completeness] "that he is more righteous than God" vs "ὅτι οὗτος δικαιότερός ἐστι τοῦ Θεοῦ": Greek 'that this one is more-righteous than the God'; English drops 'this one' (οὗτος), making 'he' ambiguous; [agency] "he was justly accusing those others" vs "ἐκείνοις δὲ δικαίως ἐνεκάλει": Greek 'to-those but justly he-was-accusing'; subject is Job (from context), but English 'he' ambiguous; more critically, ἐνεκάλει is imperfect 'was accusing', English correct; [completeness] "having betrayed God's side and denied it" vs "προσδεδωκόσι τοῦ Θεοῦ τὸ μέρος καὶ ἠρνημένοις": Greek 'having-betrayed the of-God the part and having-denied'; English 'denied it' adds 'it' not in Greek; [scripture] ""I will speak, so that I may rest, opening my lips" (Job 32:20)" vs "Λαλήσω, ἵνα ἀναπαύσωμαι ἀνοίξας τὰ χείλη": Greek has no chapter/verse marker at this point in source; English supplies Job 32:20 which is correct reference but not in this source passage; [completeness] "The person who has an intelligent hearer" vs "Ὁ τυγχάνων συνετοῦ ἀκροατοῦ": Greek 'The one obtaining intelligent hearer'; English 'has' for τυγχάνων acceptable but 'person' added; [completeness] "as if emptying and casting off the excess" vs "τὴν περιττότητα οἷον κενώσας καὶ ἀποβάλλων": Greek 'the excess as-it-were having-emptied and casting-off'; English 'as if' for οἷον acceptable, but 'and says' is added not in Greek; [completeness] "and says, "I will speak, so that I may rest."" vs "καὶ λέγει· Λαλήσω ἵνα ἀναπαύσωμαι": English adds this as separate quotation but it's in the source; third person, not second person; [modality] ""Because He will no longer set anything upon a man"" vs "Ὅτι οὐκ ἐπ' ἄνδρα θήσει ἔτι": Missing 'anything' (τι); verb is simple future 'he will set,' not 'will set anything'; [agency] ""Because to the strong one who says"" vs "Ὅτι πρὸς τὸν ἰσχυρὸν ὁ λέγων": ὁ λέγων is 'the one saying,' not 'who says'; article+participle as substantive; [completeness] "Symmachus rendered it this way: "I have taken up a speech for God; [modality] ""I will not hold back, [but will go on] unhindered"" vs "οὐχ ἕξω ἀκωλύτως": οὐχ ἕξω is 'I will not have,' not 'I will not hold back'; different verb entirely; [agency] "And he understood it this way, that is:" vs "Ὁ δὲ ἐνόησεν οὕτως, τουτέστιν": Ὁ δὲ refers to Symmachus (the translator), not Elihu; ambiguous 'he' misleads | part 4/5: [agency] "Symmachus rendered it this way" vs "ἐπειδὴ τὴν ὑπὲρ Θεοῦ ῥῆσιν ἀνέλαβον, φησὶν Ἐλιοὺς": Greek has Elihu speaking, not Symmachus rendering; Symmachus attribution is editorial insertion;
